name: Sarojini Nagar
character: Delhi's export-surplus temple. The same tops that sit in mall windows at four figures land here for a couple hundred - if you can dig, walk the back lanes, and hold your nerve while bargaining.

timings.best: weekday late mornings; skip Sunday crush

tips: The fixed-price front shops facing the main road carry the tourist markup - the real prices are in the export back-lanes.
Carry cash in small notes and a jhola; most stalls aren't on UPI and a big note invites a 'no change' round-up.
Quote 40% of the first ask and settle around 55-60%; walk once and the price usually follows you.

sections.name: Export back-lanes
sections.notes: Surplus tops, dresses, denim off the export floor - the lowest prices in the market if you dig.

sections.name: Fixed-price front shops
sections.notes: Road-facing shops; convenient but marked up - bargain hard or move inside.

sections.name: Winter corner
sections.notes: Jackets, sweaters and thermals stacked seasonally near the back.

guides.quality_note: Check for export tags cut off and small stitching defects - that's why it's cheap.

guides.bargaining_note: Start at 300 for a pair; sizing runs inconsistent, try or measure.
guides.quality_note: Zippers and stitching vary lot to lot - inspect before you pay.

guides.bargaining_note: Puffer jackets settle ~800-900 late in season.
guides.quality_note: Fill quality varies; press the jacket to feel the loft.

guides.bargaining_note: Kurtis from 250; sets cost more, bargain per piece.

name: Lajpat Nagar Central Market
character: The go-to for suits, salwar-kameez and everyday ethnic at prices that undercut every boutique. Louder and more mainstream than Sarojini, strong on tailoring, juttis and mehendi.
tips: Get unstitched suit fabric here and stitch at one of the market tailors - far cheaper than a readymade set.
The mehendi artists on the central lane are a fixed-rate institution around festival season - agree the price before they start.
Footwear prices firm up fast; bargain across two or three shops before committing.

sections.name: Central Market lane
sections.notes: Suits, dupattas, readymade kurtis - the spine of the market.

sections.name: Pushpa Market
sections.notes: Juttis, sandals, bags at haggling prices.

guides.bargaining_note: Unstitched suits from ~400; readymade sets cost more.
guides.quality_note: Check fabric weight for summer vs winter suits.

guides.bargaining_note: Juttis settle ~400-500; quote low and cross-check shops.
guides.quality_note: Check sole gluing on cheaper juttis.

name: Karol Bagh
character: Delhi's wedding-shopping engine. Ajmal Khan Road for everyday fashion and shoes, the bylanes for lehengas and sherwanis - big-ticket bridal at a fraction of designer boutiques if you know where to push.

timings.best: weekday mornings before the wedding-season crowds

tips: Bridal lehenga prices have huge headroom - never take the first quote, and shop three stores before deciding.
Ajmal Khan Road is the pedestrian fashion stretch; the heavy bridal work is in the inner lanes.
Ask for the 'without bill' price and then decide - many stores quote two numbers.

sections.name: Ajmal Khan Road
sections.notes: Everyday fashion, footwear, accessories - pedestrianised and busy.

sections.name: Bridal bylanes
sections.notes: Lehengas, sherwanis, heavy ethnic - big-ticket, big bargaining.

guides.bargaining_note: Enormous headroom - settle 40-55% of the first quote after visiting several shops.
guides.quality_note: Inspect zari and lining; heavy work hides shortcuts.

guides.bargaining_note: Ajmal Khan shoe shops bargain to ~700-800.
Quote low on Ajmal Khan Road; the fixed-price chains won't move.

name: Nehru Place
character: Asia's largest computer market - refurb laptops, every cable and adapter you can name, on-the-spot repairs and software. Prices are keen but so are the grey-market traps; know the model number before you go.
tips: Know the exact model and current online price before you walk in - it's your only anchor against a confident quote.
Refurb laptops are real value but insist on a written warranty and test the battery health before paying.
Cables and adapters are cheapest one lane in from the plaza, not at the front stalls.

sections.name: Laptop lanes
sections.notes: New, refurb and spares - the core of the market.

sections.name: Accessories & repairs
sections.notes: Cables, adapters, screen and battery repairs while you wait.

guides.bargaining_note: Cables/adapters bargain to half the front-stall quote one lane in.
guides.quality_note: Avoid unbranded chargers for laptops - buy a known brand.

guides.bargaining_note: Refurb prices move ~10-15%; anchor on the online price of the exact model.
guides.quality_note: Demand written warranty; check battery health and hinge.

guides.bargaining_note: Get two quotes; screen/battery swaps vary widely by model.
guides.quality_note: Confirm the part is genuine or clearly labelled compatible.

name: Chandni Chowk
character: The old city's wholesale heart. Kinari Bazaar for zari, laces and wedding trims; Katra Neel for fabrics by the metre; lehengas and sherwanis at wholesale prices if you can navigate the crush.

timings.best: weekday mornings; avoid the afternoon crush

tips: Go early - the lanes are impassable by afternoon and shops that let you browse in peace at 11am won't at 4pm.
Kinari Bazaar is trims and zari by the piece; buy fabric a lane over in Katra Neel and get it stitched.
Many shops are wholesale-minded - buying a few pieces gets a better rate than a single one.

sections.name: Kinari Bazaar
sections.notes: Zari, laces, tassels and wedding trims by the piece.

sections.name: Katra Neel
sections.notes: Fabrics by the metre - the fabric wholesale spine.

guides.bargaining_note: Per-metre rates drop when you buy a few metres; ask the wholesale rate.
guides.quality_note: Check colourfastness and weave before committing a full suit's worth.

guides.bargaining_note: Priced per metre/piece; buying a bundle gets a better rate.
Wholesale-leaning; settle well below the first quote, and buy where they let you inspect the work.
guides.quality_note: Check zari and lining on heavy lehengas.
